## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.
- [ ] Fallback behaviour preserved: with no usable base the function still returns `None` and callers fall back to full scope (no crash).
- [ ] Documentation updated where the changed-scope base semantics are described (`skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`) if the returned value's contract changes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Probe/read-only of git state; no new runtime dependencies; reuse existing helpers (`_git_inspection_env`, `run_cmd`).
- Behaviour change must be conservative: an unresolved base must still fall back to full scope rather than an empty diff.
- Related but distinct from SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66 (unqualified `origin/dev` ref *ambiguity* with a shadowing local branch) — both live in the same function, so either item may be implemented first; if both are taken together, keep the two fixes as separate commits.
- All written output in UK English.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_resolve_merge_base()` must return the merge-base SHA; `compute_changed_files()` consumes it unchanged.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — `TestComputeChangedFiles` gains the stale-base regression test (reuse the existing `_make_repo` fixture and `shared.git_sandbox` helpers).
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — changed-scope base semantics ("Scope-aware execution").
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — section 2 ("Scope-aware execution") states how the diff base is resolved.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ` — Main-checkout local dev diverged from origin/dev (the stale-base incident; records this hand-off).
- `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` — Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous (adjacent defect in the same function).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRMB6P6M008H4U4** – Fix legacy skill/ path reference in planall SKILL.md (completed)
- **SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX** – Fork start worktree from origin/<parent> when local is behind (blocked)
- **SA-0MVV2R1SO0025289** – [test-failure] tests/test_refactor/test_project_name.py::TestReportHeading::test_heading_uses_directory_fallback — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: acceptance, actually, adjacent, agent, agents (+175 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, adjacent, agent, agents (+171 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, actually, agent, agents, ambiguous (+169 more)

## Plan: review summary (plan skill, 2026-11-16)

The effort/risk pre-check returned **Small** / **Low**, so decomposition was skipped: this is a single vertical slice (one function fix + regression test + doc confirmation) and needs no child items.

- **Requirements & AC alignment** — every AC traces to the Problem/Evidence section; no invented ACs. The documentation AC is correctly conditional: neither `skill/test/SKILL.md` nor `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents `_resolve_merge_base()`'s return value — they state only that the merge-base is resolved automatically — so the AC is satisfied by confirming the docs need no change (or a one-line clarification if the wording is misleading).
- **Completeness** — required fields (description, ACs) present; the **Key Files:** block was normalised to valid, existing paths (the previous `skill/test/tests/` entry had no file extension).
- **Sequencing & dependencies** — no children and no dependency edges needed; the test → fix → doc-check order is enforced inside the single item.
- **Scope sizing** — one minimal end-to-end increment; no phasing required.
- **Acceptance & testability** — each AC is pass/fail verifiable through `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` and a `--scope changed` run in a stale-base fixture.
- **Polish & handoff** — actionable as-is; the existing `TestComputeChangedFiles` fixtures and `shared.git_sandbox` helpers (`init_repo`, `commit_all`, `run_git`) are the reuse candidates.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the description already carried measurable acceptance criteria, observed evidence and the exact defect location, so the plan skill auto-completed after the six review stages. Duplicate check performed with `wl search "changed scope base ref"` / `"merge base changed scope"` — no overlapping item found; `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` is the adjacent, distinct ref-ambiguity defect in the same function.

# Intake Brief — Move the detailed descriptions of the metrics into an appendix (SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS)

## Problem statement

The usage report produced by the `proxy-usage-analysis` skill (`report.md`)
interleaves the raw generated data with long descriptive prose explaining each
metric. The report opens with a header bullet block and detailed metric
explanations (availability-state footnote, total-tokens formula, busy-time
methodology, slot-seconds semantics, engine-cross-check caveats, …), so an
operator cannot read the day's numbers "at a glance" and the descriptive text
drowns the data. The detailed metric descriptions should move to an appendix
at the end of the document, the main body should contain only the data
generated (tables plus at most a one-sentence reminder of each metric's
definition), and the appendix should carry an equivalent description for
**all** metrics in the report. This item is merged with
**LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3** ("Performance metrics in usage report"), so it also
delivers that item's first-section scorecard (metrics with baseline, target,
actual, met/unmet) and its per-metric detail content (why important, how
calculated, levers, trade-offs) — which now lives in the appendix.

## Users

- **Proxy operators / the producer** — want an "at a glance" view of how well
  the local LLMs are performing (optimisation of use and amount of content
  processed) without wading through methodology prose.
- **Engineers and agents** — want a detailed breakdown of each top-level
  measure (definition, calculation, levers, trade-offs) to improve the
  numbers.

User stories:

- As an operator, I open the usage report and immediately see the data tables
  and a top-of-report scorecard (metric, baseline, target, actual, met/unmet),
  so I can tell at a glance whether local LLM usage is healthy.
- As an operator, I can find a one-sentence reminder of what each metric means
  next to its table, without the full methodology.
- As an engineer/agent, I can open a metric-glossary appendix at the end of
  the report and read, for every metric in the report, why it matters, how it
  is calculated, and what levers/trade-offs exist to improve it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The generated `report.md` main body contains only data generated
  (tables/graphs and section headers); every detailed metric-description
  passage currently embedded in the body (header block, `## Summary by hour`
  availability footnote, `## Total tokens` prose, `## Local model
  utilization` "Busy = …"/"Method:" paragraphs, `## Prefill vs decode`
  slot-seconds explanation, `## Engine cross-check` caveats, and any similar
  inline prose in other sections) moves to an appendix at the end of the
  document.
- AC2: Each metric in the main body is accompanied by at most a **one-sentence
  reminder** of its definition (e.g. a short gloss next to the table or under
  the section header); a reminder is present for every metrics table whose
  full description moved to the appendix.
- AC3: A metric-glossary appendix (`## Appendix: Metric definitions` or
  equivalent) at the end of `report.md` contains an entry for **every metric
  in the report** (per producer answer Q2=A — full glossary): definition,
  why it matters, how it is calculated, and — for the performance/scorecard
  metrics — levers and trade-offs (LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 content).
- AC4: A top-of-report scorecard section (metrics, baseline, target, actual,
  met/unmet observation) is added per LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3, built from the
  validation work items' measured figures; every scorecard metric has its
  detail entry in the appendix (not duplicated in the body).
- AC5: While building the appendix, opportunities to improve the report were
  considered — any metric added, removed, or restructured is documented in the
  work-item description or a follow-on item; the report keeps its two intended
  uses (at-a-glance data + detailed breakdown).
- AC6: The `report.md` still renders for every window shape (empty window,
  zero-traffic, no llama-server logs, GPU data absent) without errors, and the
  existing per-section regression tests are updated where section content
  changed (full project test suite passes).
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries for `proxy-usage-analysis`.

## Constraints

- Implementation lives in the **llm-manager** project
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`); tracking/worklog is in SorraAgents
  (cross-repo pattern per SA-0MTM3LKP1003S28J — commit on llm-manager `dev`).
- The pipeline stays fully deterministic and rule-based (no LLM in the
  report); changing the report must not change the proxy, the parser, or the
  `--json` summary keys.
- The daily 05:00 cron path (agent-free) must keep working unchanged; the
  report layout change must not break `cron.log` or archival.
- The one-sentence reminder rule: descriptions shorten, never bloat the body;
  the appendix is the single home for detail (producer Q1=C, Q3=A).

Ruff reports `ISC004` ("Unparenthesized implicit string concatenation in collection") at `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py:712-716`. A five-part f-string is deliberately concatenated at compile time into a single `corpus: ...` list entry in `render_summary()`; the comma at line 716 is the list-element separator. ## Goal

As an agent auditing a work item at a freshly pushed `dev` HEAD, I want the audit's full-suite evidence check to reuse the tree-keyed verdict the dev-push gate just recorded for that same commit, so the first audit after every push does not pay for a second identical full-suite run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG` (shipped `39ea226b4`) re-keyed the dev-push pre-push gate to the pushed commit's **tree** (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`, `git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}`). The gate therefore no longer writes a loose-worktree-keyed entry for the pushed commit.

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_classify_full_suite_cache` still queries the cache worktree-only (`query_cached(command, cwd=..., ttl=AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)`), following the documented contract in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.3 ("callers that pass nothing keep the historical worktree keys byte for byte (test-skill CLI, audit)").

Consequence, observed live during this epic's own audit at HEAD `ea89bb4e2`:

```
Automatic full-suite verification unavailable: 4 of 4 suite command(s) not verifiably green at HEAD ea89bb4e2 …
```

The gate had already gated that exact commit, yet the audit could not see the verdict and re-executed the whole suite (4 commands, several minutes). Before the tree keying, the gate's worktree-keyed run was mirrored into the main checkout cache and served the audit. This is the mirror image of the reuse gap `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` closed for finish → pre-push, now on the audit path.

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` already solved the identical problem for its own post-push verification (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`, `54d5b79f1`): resolve the pushed commit's tree, query `fingerprint_kind="tree"` first, then fall back to the loose worktree key. The audit path needs the same treatment.

## Desired change

- `_classify_full_suite_cache` (the single full-suite classifier behind `_auto_green_run_outcome` / `_resolve_auto_green_run` and the F3 auto-execution path) resolves the audited HEAD's tree (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`, via a helper mirroring `implement.py`'s `_resolve_commit_tree`) and queries the tree-kind entry **first**, falling back to the historical worktree query so legacy entries still count. Out of scope, deliberately: `_classify_herdr_suite_cache` (a herdr profile is never full-suite evidence by its own contract) and `_cached_red_failures` (red-diagnostics only; a red entry never satisfies evidence and the caller executes fresh).
- A tree-kind entry accepted as evidence is reported with its `fingerprint_kind` and age, so a reused verdict is visible in the audit output rather than implied.
- `query_cached()`'s worktree-only default is unchanged for every other caller (the finish gate's staged-tree semantics depend on it).

## Acceptance criteria

1. An audit at a HEAD whose only cached full-suite evidence is tree-kind (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`, keyed on `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`) reports full-suite evidence **without executing** the suite.
2. A worktree-kind (legacy) entry at the audited HEAD is still accepted, byte-for-byte keying unchanged.
3. An entry recorded for a *different* tree is a miss (a green verdict for another tree is never accepted).
4. The reused verdict's `fingerprint_kind` and age are reported in the audit output/JSON.
5. Deterministic tests cover: tree-kind hit (no execution), legacy worktree hit, different-tree miss, and the unchanged `query_cached()` default for other callers.
6. Documentation is updated: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.3/§0.4 and the audit-side note in `docs/dev/` describing the audit's evidence query, corrected from "worktree only" to "tree-kind first, worktree fallback".
7. Every new behaviour is exercised by an automated test executed through the test skill, and the full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_classify_full_suite_cache` (the single full-suite classifier) and its `_auto_green_run_outcome` / F3 callers.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `query_cached(fingerprint=…, fingerprint_kind=…)` (already supports the tree kind; no new API expected).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the `_resolve_post_push_verification` precedent (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`) to mirror.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — §0.3/§0.4 contract correction.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_green_run.py` — the audit full-suite cache test home (new tree-kind reuse tests live here or in a sibling module).

## Impact

An agent auditing work at a freshly pushed `dev` HEAD reuses the gate's tree-keyed green verdict instead of re-running the same full suite, cutting the first audit after each push by roughly one full-suite execution.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN** – [test-failure] post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** – finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly (completed)
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** – Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mw7c6bmz00931jg, 0mwaxc5td00461fn, acceptance, accepted, age (+163 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mw7c6bmz00931jg, 0mwaxc5td00461fn, acceptance, accepted, age (+163 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, accepted, age, agent, already (+161 more)

# Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Test-first tracer bullet: write the regression tests **before** the fix. Expectations that
target the new behaviour carry `xfail(strict=True)` until the implementation child removes
the marker; expectations that already hold (the conservative failure paths, the
ancestry-not-equality rule) pass before and after, so a failing test can only be failing on
the behaviour under test.

## Goal

As an implementation agent, I want hermetic, deterministic tests that pin the remote-observed
push verdict, so a later change to `finish`'s push-outcome handling can never silently regress
into reporting a landed push as a failure — nor into claiming success for a commit that never
reached `origin/dev`.

## Context

`finish` treats the exit status of `git push` as the sole verdict on whether the commit reached
`origin/dev`, so a push interrupted after the remote accepted the ref (timeout, process-group
kill, late non-zero exit) is reported as a failure and the item is reset to `open`. The only
remote check today is the post-*success* ancestry assertion
(`_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()`, `implement.py` L8084), which runs after a push already
claimed success — nothing distinguishes "landed but interrupted" from "never landed". No
existing test simulates the race: `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py`,
`tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` all assume the push verdict is truthful.

## Scope

Tests only — no production-code change in this slice. Deliver the failing baselines that the
implementation child turns green, plus the companion tests that prove the preconditions (a
real hermetic push, a reachable bare remote, a real terminal read-back) rather than assuming
them.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — new hermetic suite: probe variants, the three outcomes, sibling-push ancestry.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — existing interrupted-push coverage; extend where a case belongs there.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push baseline (a retry that lands but is reported as failed).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — reusable `init_bare_remote` / `init_repo` / `add_worktree` / `commit_all` factories; reuse rather than hand-rolling fixtures.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the `FakeGitBoundary` stubbed-boundary harness style for end-to-end `phase_finish` tests.

## Constraints

- **Hermetic:** self-contained bare remote plus clone/worktree under `tmp_path`; never mutate the live checkout's refs, never touch the shared `refs/heads/dev`, no network access.
- **Unambiguous baselines:** pair each new-behaviour `xfail(strict=True)` with a companion that passes before and after, so the preconditions are proven separately instead of being smuggled into the baseline.
- **No hiding failures:** `xfail(strict=True)` only where the expectation targets the not-yet-implemented behaviour.
- **Test execution policy:** no agent-initiated `pytest`/`run_tests.py` invocation outside `/skill:test` (`implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate and the dev-push gate are infrastructure and out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Interrupted push variants are covered by unit tests.** Unit tests drive each interrupted-push variant — `PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, and a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward — and assert the remote verification probe runs before any push failure is reported: it verifies whether the commit being pushed is reachable from the remote `dev` tip (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` plus a fetch of that ref and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>`), is time-bounded, uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite), and applies to the non-fast-forward retry push as well as the first push.
- **Verified-landed success end-to-end.** An end-to-end hermetic test against a bare remote plus a clone under `tmp_path` — where the remote already contains the commit and the push hangs past a short timeout — asserts `report["success"] is True`, the push step is marked `verified_after_failure`, the completion comment naming the commit is posted, the existing success-path cleanup runs (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), and the work item is `completed`/`in_review` with the terminal read-back still passing.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome are distinguished.** Negative tests — a remote without the commit, and a verification probe that itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error) — assert `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Hermetic regression coverage, ancestry not equality.** The new tests are hermetic (self-contained bare remote plus clone under `tmp_path`; no live checkout or live `refs/heads/dev` mutation, no network access) and cover an interrupted push that landed, an interrupted push that did not land, a verification probe failure, and a sibling push advancing `origin/dev` after ours (ancestry, not equality, must be accepted); they fail without the fix (or exercise the new helper directly) and pass with it, reusing the `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` factories.
data.title: Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests

# Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite

## Goal

Add the failing-first regression tests for the stale-branch half of
SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G (AC3/AC4) so the implementation children have a pinned
contract. The tree stays green: every new test is marked
`pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` naming
SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G while the behaviour is absent, and the implementation
children remove the markers when the behaviour lands — a `strict=True`
`xpass` is a hard failure, so a marker can never be forgotten.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command — pinned here by a regression test.
- `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures — pinned here by a regression test over the extended contract.
- A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed — pinned here by regression tests.
- Regression tests cover `git_worktree_add` / `phase_start` stale-branch handling (reuse, fast-forward, actionable error, cleanup).
- Every new test is marked `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` in this item so the suite is green on landing; the implementing children flip the markers to normal passing tests.
- Tests build their own scratch git repository under `tmp_path` (no network, no writes outside it) and assert the concrete report field they will consume (`reused_branch`, `branch_fast_forwarded`, the named-branch error text, `branch_removed` / `branch_retained`) rather than only that an exception was raised.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- New test module `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` mirroring the
  module-loading fixture in `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`.
- Extend `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py` (reuse/fast-forward/actionable
  error on an existing branch) and `tests/test_implement_abort_safety.py`
  (branch removal, and retention when the branch carries the only copy of a
  commit) where their existing harness already fits.
- Reuse `shared.git_sandbox.init_repo` / `run_git` to create the three branch
  states: identical to the parent branch, strictly behind it, and carrying a
  unique commit.
- Each test names SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G in its `xfail` reason so the marker is
  self-documenting and grep-able.

## Constraints

- Do not modify production code in this item (tests only).
- The suite must be green when this item finishes (xfail-marked tests are
  reported as xfailed, not failures).

# Recover guarded-child delegation guard

## Goal

Restore the `do-not-delegate` guard in `implement.py` automatic parent
recursion. A complete implementation, test suite and docs edit already exist
in the recoverable commit `91c9b44d1` (from the now-deleted subset item
SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876); this child replays that work onto the current tree
rather than re-deriving it.

Provenance: `git show 91c9b44d1` — files
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`,
`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` (612 lines).
Its base `c818324b1` is an ancestor of `dev`, so it replays cleanly except
for one deliberate adaptation (below).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py parent` treats a child tagged `do-not-delegate` as not startable: `_classify_child` returns a dedicated guarded classification (`skip-do-not-delegate`), and both `_next_child_to_implement` and the `phase_parent` child loop skip it, reporting it in the parent report with a distinct action (`"skipped-do-not-delegate"`) and no dependency-`blocked` masking.
- Guarded children are never started, claimed, or re-attempted by `parent`; startable siblings still proceed, and a guarded child is never advanced past (guarded is not terminal, so the parent does not complete while guarded children remain).
- Direct `implement.py start <child>` / `drive <child>` on a `do-not-delegate` child continues to work (that explicit invocation is the documented override); only automatic parent recursion is gated.
- `phase_drive` spawns no session for a guarded child and forwards `guarded_children` for parity with `phase_parent`.
- Guard precedence is adapted to the current tree: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-do-not-delegate` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`, so a `blocked` child is never masked as guarded (nor guarded as `blocked`).
- Regression tests cover `_classify_child` / `_next_child_to_implement` with `do-not-delegate` children (guarded skipped, siblings still selected, override path unaffected).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` is present and passing against the current tree, and the existing parent-recursion/dependency test suites still pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Replay the guarded-child hunks of `91c9b44d1`: `DO_NOT_DELEGATE_TAG`,
  `ACTION_SKIP_DO_NOT_DELEGATE`, `ACTION_SKIPPED_DO_NOT_DELEGATE`,
  `_has_do_not_delegate_tag()`, and the `_classify_child` branch.
- Insert the guard **before** the `blocked` branch in `_classify_child`
  (the recovered commit predates `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED`); `_classify_child`
  keeps its current `(child, blockers, children)` signature.
- Port the `_next_child_to_implement` skip and the `phase_parent` child-loop
  branch (`guarded_ids`, `children_processed` entry, `guarded_children`
  report field, guarded-specific waiting message) and the `phase_drive`
  forwarding.
- Restore the recovered tests, then add one test pinning the new precedence
  (a guarded child that is also `status: blocked` classifies as guarded).
- Restore the recovered `SKILL.md` / reference-doc guard paragraphs; the docs
  child later owns the stale-branch documentation.

## Constraints

- Replay, do not blind-cherry-pick: `git show 91c9b44d1 -- <path>` is the
  source of truth; resolve the intervening changes by hand and keep the
  current file's style and docstrings.
- No behaviour change for terminal, held, in-progress, blocked or plain
  startable children.
- Idempotent: re-running `parent` on a guarded child performs no claim, no
  worktree creation, no status/stage write and emits the same report.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_has_do_not_delegate_tag`, `_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `phase_parent`, `phase_drive`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` (recovered)

## Dependencies

- None. Independent of the stale-branch children.

## Deliverables

- `do-not-delegate` classification wired through parent/drive selection.
- `guarded_children` / `skipped-do-not-delegate` reporting.
- Recovered 612-line regression suite plus a guarded-vs-blocked precedence test.

# Problem Statement

Ruff rule `RUF059` ("Unpacked variable ... is never used") flags three names
bound by the tuple unpack on line 118 of `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py`:
`mode`, `uid` and `gid`. The work item names only `mode` because it was the
first diagnostic reported, but one fix at that line clears all three.

# Users

- **Test maintainer / any developer running ruff on this repo**: wants the lint
  output for the test suite to be trustworthy, so a real finding is not buried
  under dead bindings in a test that is otherwise clean.

Example user story: *As a developer running ruff over `tests/`, I want
`tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` to report no unused-binding findings, so I
can treat a red lint run as a genuine regression.*

# Acceptance Criteria

1. The tuple unpack on line 118 of `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` no longer
   binds unused names, so `ruff check --select RUF059 tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py`
   reports zero findings for that line (covers all three reported names:
   `mode`, `uid`, `gid`).
2. Test behaviour is unchanged: `test_template_has_valid_tmpfiles_lines` still
   asserts the six-field count (`type path mode uid gid age`) and the ≥1-day
   age threshold, and `age` still carries the value of `fields[5]`.
3. Validation: `pytest tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` (run through the test
   skill) passes with the change.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

# Impact

Developers running lint over the test suite get a clean RUF059 signal from this
file again, so a genuine unused-binding regression elsewhere is no longer
masked by known noise here.

# Constraints

- Single-line change inside `test_template_has_valid_tmpfiles_lines`; no
  behavioural change and no assertion may be added, removed or weakened.
- The field-count assertion (`len(fields) == 6`) and the age parsing/`>= 86400`
  check must stay exactly as they are.
- Out of scope (see Risks): strengthening the test to validate `mode`/`uid`/
  `gid` values, despite the docstring's "sane values" claim — that is a
  behavioural change to the test, not a lint fix.
- Do not remove the `REFACTOR-SA-0MWDV1YYV007K5EA` marker comment at the top of
  the file: markers are the refactor skill's duplicate-filing guard, and the
  precedent item (SA-0MWDV1XHW005Y6J5) left its own marker in place.
- Rust/ruff version: the diagnostic is reproducible with the ruff available in
  this environment (`ruff check --select RUF059`, 3 findings at line 118).

# Existing state

```python
        fields = line.split()
        rule_type, _ = fields[0], fields[1]   # line 100: F841 already fixed
        ...
        _, _, mode, uid, gid, age = fields    # line 118: RUF059 x3
```

Only `age` is used downstream (the age-threshold assertion). `mode`, `uid` and
`gid` are bound and never read; the surrounding comment
`# AC1: age >= 1 day; ...` confirms `age` is the only intended consumer.

# Desired change

```python
        age = fields[5]
```

Rationale: mirrors the file's existing indexing style one screen above
(`rule_type, _ = fields[0], fields[1]`), keeps the field-order comment
(`type path mode uid gid age`) truthful, and removes all three dead bindings in
one edit.

Alternative considered and rejected: `_, _, _, _, _, age = fields` — correct
but noisier than the indexing form already used in the same function.

The stale RUF059 marker comment at the top of the file is left untouched (see
Constraints).

# Key Files

- `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` — line 118, single-line refactor inside
  `test_template_has_valid_tmpfiles_lines`; the test body and assertions are
  otherwise untouched.

# Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: the item's "line 100" refers to the file state at scan time;
  the diagnostic is now at line 118 after intervening commits. The marker
  comment `# <!-- REFACTOR-SA-0MWDV1YYV007K5EA ... -->` in the file header
  confirms the identity, so line-number drift is not a blocker.
- **Risk (scope creep)**: the test docstring claims "sane values" but only age
  is validated. Tempting to add mode/uid/gid assertions while touching the
  line; deliberately excluded — record as a follow-up work item if wanted.
- **Risk (behavioural drift)**: replacing the unpack with `fields[5]` silently
  depends on field order; mitigated by keeping the field-order comment and the
  existing six-field assertion, and by AC2.
- **Risk (conflict)**: SA-0MWDV20G7008ZORK edits a different hunk (~line 167,
  `subprocess.run` `check` argument) of the same file — no merge conflict
  expected.

# Related work

- **SA-0MWDV1XHW005Y6J5** (completed) — same file, F841 unused local `path`;
  established the `_`/indexing convention and the description structure reused
  here.
- **SA-0MWDV20G7008ZORK** (open, stage `idea`) — same file, `subprocess.run`
  without explicit `check` (PLW1510); another linter fix in the same test.
- **SA-0MW2QEZBG009I3AI** — original item that introduced
  `tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py` and `scripts/pi-test-tmp.conf`.

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the seed context plus repository search was sufficient to
draft a complete brief.

Research summary: `ruff check --select RUF059 tests/test_tmp_inode_headroom.py`
reproduces three findings at line 118 (`mode`, `uid`, `gid`), all from the same
unpack; `wl search "ruff_specific test_tmp_inode_headroom"` returned only this
item (no duplicate), and `wl show` on the two other `REFACTOR-*` markers in the
file identified one completed precedent (SA-0MWDV1XHW005Y6J5) and one open
sibling (SA-0MWDV20G7008ZORK), neither of which covers this RUF059 finding.
The repo carries no ruff configuration file (`ruff.toml`/`pyproject.toml`), so
the finding comes from the refactor skill's ruff invocation
(`skill/refactor/smell_detection.py`) rather than project lint defaults.

# Report summary line should match the skill that produced it

## Problem statement

Every end-of-session report closes with a hardcoded `✅ Ready to ship` (green) or `🚫 Not ready to ship` (red) Conclusion line, no matter which skill produced the report. All 16 skills that call `render_report.py` — plan, intake, implement, audit, test, ship, refactor, cleanup, triage, etc. — say "Ready to ship", which is only accurate for the audit/ship skills and actively misleading for the rest (e.g. intake's report claiming the work item is ready to ship before planning has even happened).

## Users

Primary users are the **producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports, and the **agents** whose final message renders the report.

- As a producer, I want the closing line of a report to reflect what the skill actually accomplished, so I can tell at a glance whether a stage genuinely finished.
- As an agent, I want the verdict line I render to be accurate for the skill I ran, so my final message is not misleading.

## Impact

Producers can tell at a glance, from the very last line of any session report, exactly which stage completed (or failed) and what the work item is ready for next — no more generic "Ready to ship" from an intake or plan session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `render_report.py` renders a per-skill summary line on success — plan → "Plan complete", intake → "Intake complete", implement → "Ready for audit", audit → "Ready to ship" (unchanged), and a sensible drafted line for each remaining skill (full mapping in Desired change). Unknown/unmapped `skill_name` falls back to today's "Ready to ship" (backward compatible).
- AC2: The failure line mirrors its skill's success line (e.g. implement → "Not ready for audit", intake → "Intake incomplete"), preserving the red colouring and the closing "This completes the <skill> process for <id> (<title>)." sentence.
- AC3: Every skill that invokes `render_report.py` (all 16 SKILL.md call sites) renders its own line without further per-skill changes — the mapping lives in the renderer keyed by `skill_name` (case-insensitive).
- AC4: Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` docs and the golden-report examples so the documented Conclusion matches the new per-skill behaviour; README/wiki entries referencing the conclusion line are updated.
- AC5: `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` covers the mapping: at least one happy-path per skill or a table-driven parametrised test, one failure-line case, one unknown-skill fallback case, and the existing "Ready to ship" assertions updated to the new expectations.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve colour behaviour (`colour_enabled` auto-detection and `--colour`/`--no-colour` overrides) as-is; only the words change, not the colour logic.
- Keep the Conclusion wording backward compatible: any skill not in the mapping (e.g. future skills) must still get today's "Ready to ship" line rather than erroring.
- Do not alter the header line (`# Completed <skill>`), AC table, or Meta-Data sections — only the Conclusion verdict line(s).

## Existing state

`render_report.py` Conclusion section (lines ~604–618) hardcodes:

- success: `✅ Ready to ship` + "This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title})."
- failure: `🚫 Not ready to ship` + "{Skill} session for {id} ({title}) is incomplete."

The `skill_name` parameter is already passed by every caller (16 SKILL.md call sites, verified by grep) and is already used in the header and the closing sentence — only the verdict line ignores it.

## Desired change

Add a per-skill mapping (draft; operator to confirm during review) in `render_report.py`:

| skill_name | success line | failure line |
|---|---|---|
| plan | Plan complete | Plan incomplete |
| intake | Intake complete | Intake incomplete |
| implement | Ready for audit | Not ready for audit |
| audit | Ready to ship | Not ready to ship |
| ship | Released to dev | Release incomplete |
| test | All tests passed | Tests failed/incomplete |
| refactor | Refactor complete | Refactor incomplete |
| cleanup | Cleanup complete | Cleanup incomplete |
| triage | Triage complete | Triage incomplete |
| code-review | Review complete | Review incomplete |
| author-command | Command authored | Command authoring incomplete |
| resolve-pr-comments | PR comments resolved | PR comments incomplete |
| find-related | Related work gathered | Related work search incomplete |
| effort-and-risk | Effort and risk assessed | Effort/risk assessment incomplete |
| machine-hygiene | Hygiene check complete | Hygiene check incomplete |
| agent-log-review | Log review complete | Log review incomplete |
| *(unknown)* | Ready to ship | Not ready to ship |

Failure lines keep the existing explanatory sentence about the incomplete session.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Add the per-skill summary-line mapping and use it for the Conclusion verdict lines (lines ~604–618).
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Update "Ready to ship" assertions (~lines 586–1060) and add mapping/failure/fallback coverage.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — Update Conclusion examples (golden report shows `✅ Ready to ship`), document the mapping.
- README / docs entries referencing the conclusion line — update if present.

## Risks & assumptions

- Wording for the 12 non-example skills is an operator-approved draft (Q1=A) and remains reviewable during implementation/review; the four named lines (plan/intake/implement/audit) are fixed by the item.
- An unmapped/future skill silently receiving "Ready to ship" is mitigated by AC1's explicit fallback and by documenting the mapping in `skill/report/SKILL.md` so new skills know to extend it.
- Scope creep risk: the change is confined to the Conclusion verdict lines; header, AC table, Meta-Data and producer-actions rendering are out of scope (see Constraints) — any further report-polish ideas should be filed as separate work items.
- Assumption: "Ready to ship" wording for audit is unchanged (per item description and related item SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI), so the two items do not conflict.

## Related work

- SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI — Audit report Conclusion can claim 'Ready to ship' when the audit failed (open, high). Partial overlap on the same Conclusion section: that item gates the audit skill's "Ready to ship" on the persisted audit verdict; this item changes wording per skill. Independent changes; audit's success line stays "Ready to ship" so no text conflict. Reference as related work, not a duplicate.
- SA-0MVYEZ3V3004AQXN — Clearer audit results (completed): colour/readability foundation this builds on (colour capability preserved as a constraint).
- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S / SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L — report helper skill creation + tests (completed): origin of the renderer being changed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which skills get skill-specific summary lines?" — Answer (operator): "A — all ~16 skills that call `render_report.py`, each with its own line." Source: interactive reply. Research: grep of `--skill-name` across `skill/*/SKILL.md` shows 16 callers (agent-log-review, audit, author-command, cleanup, code-review, effort-and-risk, find-related, implement, intake, machine-hygiene, plan, refactor, resolve-pr-comments, ship, test, triage); `report` skill itself renders no report (0 call sites). Mapping drafted in Desired change for operator confirmation.
- Q2: "Should the failure line become skill-specific too?" — Answer (operator): "A — yes, mirror the success line per skill." Source: interactive reply. Failure lines drafted as "Not <success>" / "<skill> incomplete" variants above; accepted pattern to confirm at review.

## Context

Child of **SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU** (Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects). Implements parent **AC4** (dated, idempotent scheduled output) and **AC5** (failures surfaced, never a silent success). Producer decisions Q1–Q3 are settled in the parent brief: per-project `/skill:test-churn` entries, checked-in managed-root list, 7-day default interval.

## Scope

A thin, deterministic wrapper over the existing analyser
(`skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`) that a scheduled
`/skill:test-churn` run invokes, so a scheduled run cannot drift from the
documented output contract. The wrapper owns path resolution and exit-code
propagation only — all analysis stays in the analyser (no duplicate logic).

Design decisions (documented, not open questions):

- Output is pinned to `<root>/reports/test-churn/<YYYY-MM-DD>/test_churn_report.md`
  and `test_churn_data.json`; `--report-name`/`--json-name` are not exposed by
  the wrapper so the scheduled contract cannot be re-pointed per call.
- **History is intentionally unbounded** by default (`--max-commits 0`). The
  analyser's growth metrics are whole-history by definition, so a default
  commit bound would silently change the trend. CPU cost is mitigated by the
  staggering and `priority: low` in the provisioning child, per the parent's
  CPU-blocking risk. `--since`/`--max-commits` remain pass-through options for
  constrained runs.
- `--date` is injectable so tests are clock-independent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `run_scheduled.py --root <git repo> --date 2026-11-14` writes exactly
  `reports/test-churn/2026-11-14/test_churn_report.md` and

A checked-in, reviewable list of the managed project roots plus a small loader

## Goal

Add the core classification function that determines whether a work item was auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker or manually dispatched by the operator.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: classify_auto_dispatch(item_id, window_start, window_end, worklog_dir) returns True if any of these conditions hold:
  (a) A matching entry in .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log where itemId == item_id and outcome != spawn-failed (ignore outcome field if absent — pre-enrichment entries are still valid).
  (b) A worklog comment on the item containing the prefix Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at.
  (c) A matching entry in downtime-dispatches.log with kind: scheduled (scheduled prompts count as auto-dispatch).

- [ ] AC2: Returns False (manual) for:
  (a) outcome: spawn-failed entries — not a successful dispatch.
  (b) Items found only in downtime-coordination.log or local-route.log — must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
  (c) Items with no matching dispatch log entry AND no comment marker.

- [ ] AC3: Read-side failures degrade gracefully — missing/unreadable .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log file, unparseable JSONL lines, or wl comment list failure causes the function to log a warning (stderr) and fall through to the manual bucket for that item. The function never raises.

- [ ] AC4: The dispatch log lookup uses the worklog_dir to locate the file (respects --worklog-dir / WL_WORKLOG_DIR); when no worklog_dir is set, falls back to cwd/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log.

- [ ] AC5: Unit-tested with fixtures: (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) outcome: spawn-failed entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in downtime-coordination.log / local-route.log only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

## Goal

what the test suite costs and how it has grown, so that every later prune/rework
decision in the epic is provable against numbers rather than intuition.

## Context

test-value pipeline. The epic already quotes test-churn-analyser v2.1.0 numbers
from `dev` @ `7875214`; this item refreshes them at the refactor's baseline
commit and adds the runtime and inventory dimensions the analyser does not
produce.

In-scope inventory measured at planning time (tracked files only):
431 test files — 375 pytest (`test_*.py`) and 56 node (`*.test.mjs` /
`test-*.mjs`). Per-area: `tests/` 176, `skill/audit` 64, `skill/implement` 51,
`skill/shared` 30, `skill/test` 15, `skill/standup` 12, `skill/machine-hygiene`
7, `skill/intake` 5, remaining skills ≤3 each, `command/` 1.

## Deliverables

  exact commands used, the numbers, and the caveats.
- `docs/dev/test-value-baseline.json` — machine-readable mirror of the same
  numbers (consumed by the Classify and Report children).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Enumerate the in-scope set from tracked files only:
   `git ls-files` filtered to `test_*.py`, `*.test.{mjs,js,ts}` and
   `test-*.mjs`; **exclude `.worklog/worktrees/**`** (untracked copies of the
   whole repo — 7k+ phantom test files), helpers, fixtures and setup files.
   Record the count and per-area breakdown.
2. Refresh the churn baseline with
   `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` at the baseline commit;
   record both rewrite-ratio variants with their denominators, test files/lines
   added vs deleted, net growth, and the per-quarter trend.
3. Capture suite wall-clock runtime through the test skill only
   (`run_tests.py --suite all --type full --json`, `elapsed_seconds`), once per
   suite (pytest, node) and at least twice, recording the median and the host /
   parallelism caveat. Never invoke `pytest`/`node --test` directly.
4. Capture per-file runtime if the runner already exposes it; if it does not,
   record that limitation and cross-reference `SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ` (per-test
   runtime and flakiness) rather than building a second measurement path.
5. Commit both artefacts and cite the baseline commit + analyser version.

## Goal

Update `select_group_from_changed_files` to return `frozenset[str] | None` instead of `str | None`, representing the union of **all** groups whose `paths` match at least one changed file. The iteration order must be deterministic (sorted group names).

## Problem

Currently `select_group_from_changed_files` returns a single group via `min()` — when multiple groups match a changed file, only one is returned. This causes the changed-scope gate to skip testing all other affected skill suites (SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9).

## Requirements

- Return `frozenset[str] | None` (sorted group names in the frozenset for determinism).
- All groups whose `paths` spec matches **any** changed file are included.
- Single-group match returns a frozenset with one element (backwards-compatible with callers that check `bool(result)`).
- `None` when no groups match (unchanged fallback).
- Deterministic: iteration order is sorted group names, not set-iteration order.
- `full` group is still intentionally excluded from selection.

## Impact

A cross-skill change set (e.g. touching implement + test + audit skills) now surfaces all affected groups, enabling the changed-scope gate to test every one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Changes to `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**`, and `skill/audit/**` returns `frozenset({"implement", "test", "audit"})`.
- AC2: A single-group change returns `frozenset({"audit"})` (single element).
- AC3: No matching files returns `None` (unchanged fallback).
- AC4: `full` group is never included in the returned frozenset.
- AC5: Existing single-match tests in `TestChangedFileToGroup` are updated to expect frozenset returns.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `select_group_from_changed_files` (line ~1614)
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_groups.py` — `TestChangedFileToGroup` tests

## Dependencies

- None — this is the foundational change that other children depend on.

## Goal

Update `changed_scope_selection` to iterate all matched groups (from the new multi-group `select_group_from_changed_files`), union their commands, and check outside-group files against the union of all matched groups\’s `paths`.

## Problem

`changed_scope_selection` currently calls `select_group_from_changed_files` which returns a single group, then computes outside-group files only relative to that one group. When multiple groups match, only the first groupsquo;s outside files are checked, and the otherssquo; test files are silently dropped.

## Requirements

- `ChangedScopeSelection.group` changes from `str | None` to `frozenset[str] | None`.
- `changed_scope_selection` iterates all groups in the frozenset and unions their commands.
- `_changed_outside_group_paths` is updated (or a multi-group variant added) to check changed files outside the **union** of all matched groups\’s `paths`.
- Fail-closed rule preserved: if a changed file outside all matched groups has no selectable file-level command → `commands is None` with `CHANGED_SCOPE_GROUP_INCOMPLETE`.
- A group matching multiple changed files runs once (no duplicate commands via `_union_commands`).

## Impact

A cross-skill change set that touches multiple groups now runs all affected suites in the changed-scope gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A change touching `skill/implement/**`, `skill/test/**`, `skill/audit/**` invokes all three groups\’s suite commands.
- AC2: A group matching multiple changed files runs once (no duplicate commands).
- AC3: No group match → existing fallback behaviour unchanged (file-level selection, then full).
- AC4: `selection.group` is a `frozenset[str] | None`.
- AC5: Outside-group fail-closed works across the union of matched groups.

# ruff TRY004 False-Positive Audit Waiver → resolved by refactor (Option B)

> **Decision (producer, 2026-11-17): Option B — refactor.** The producer chose
> to remove the TRY004 trigger at source rather than record an audit waiver.
> AC1/AC2 below are rewritten from the waiver shape to the refactor shape.

## Problem Statement

Ruff's **TRY004** rule (`type-check-without-type-error`) flags a *type check that
does not raise `TypeError`*. At `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:13609` the
`raise RuntimeError(...)` sits inside an `if isinstance(exc, PushTransportLostError):`
branch that dispatches between two **caught exception types**
(`PushTransportLostError` vs `PushTransportExhaustedError`) within a single
`except (PushTransportLostError, PushTransportExhaustedError) as exc:` handler
(line 13542). The `isinstance` check is **not** validating a caller's argument
type — it selects which user-facing message to emit for a transport failure.
Ruff's heuristic treats it as a failed type guard and suggests `TypeError`;
raising `TypeError` here would be semantically wrong (a lost SSH transport is
not a type error). The producer therefore chose to restructure the handler so
there is no exception-type `isinstance` for the heuristic to misfire on.

> **Correction (plan, 2026-11-17):** the original Problem Statement described
> TRY004 as `error-messages-should-include-exception-class` ("needs the
> exception-class prefix in the message"). That is **not** what TRY004 checks —
> see `ruff rule TRY004`. The false-positive characterisation is unchanged; the
> rationale is corrected so the plan targets the real heuristic.

## Users

- **Agent/operator running `implement finish`**: Needs clear, actionable messages distinguishing infrastructure failures from test failures.
- **Audit system**: Needs no further spurious TRY004 chores from this line.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `ruff check --select TRY004 skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` reports **zero** findings (currently exactly one, at line 13609).
2. The trigger is removed at source: the two `isinstance(exc, PushTransportLostError)` dispatches (verification-time lines 13555 and 13602) are eliminated by handling `PushTransportLostError` and `PushTransportExhaustedError` in a way that needs no exception-type check (split `except` clauses sharing a prelude helper), **without** changing the exception classes (`RuntimeError`) or any user-facing message text.
3. Behaviour is preserved: all existing push-transport regression tests pass **unchanged** — convergence-on-landed (`outcome: already_pushed`), `reason: connection_closed` vs `reason: transport`, `outcome: push_failed`, the transport-lost comment, the exhausted-infrastructure comment, and the two `RuntimeError` message texts.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Impact

The audit stops flagging (and stops minting chores for) a deliberate exception-type dispatch in the push error path, so `implement finish` transport handling stays lint-clean without a waiver and future audits of this file stay quiet.

## Constraints

- The exception classes (`PushTransportLostError`, `PushTransportExhaustedError`, and the re-raised `RuntimeError`) must not be changed — they semantically match transport/runtime failures.
- The user-facing message text must not be altered — it is actionable and already pinned by tests.
- The original "only the specific line is waived" constraint is **moot**: Option B records no waiver.

## Existing State

- `except (PushTransportLostError, PushTransportExhaustedError) as exc:` opens at line 13542. `PushTransportLostError` (line 5012) and `PushTransportExhaustedError` (line 5050) are **sibling** subclasses of `RuntimeError` (neither subclasses the other), so splitting into two `except` clauses is behaviour-equivalent.
- Dispatch #1 at line 13555 (`if isinstance(exc, PushTransportLostError):`) only builds `push_step` — it does not raise, so it does not trigger TRY004, but it duplicates the per-type dict literal that the split removes.
- Dispatch #2 at line 13602 (same `isinstance`) emits the transport-lost comment and `raise RuntimeError("git push to dev transport lost: ...")` at 13609 — **this** is the TRY004 trigger.
- The non-lost path emits the exhausted-infrastructure comment and `raise RuntimeError("git push to dev failed (transient transport) ...")` at 13636 — not flagged (no type check in that branch).
- Shared prelude used by both types: `push_step.update(_push_retry_trail_fields(...))`, `landed_now = _commit_is_on_origin_dev(...)` + convergence branch, `push_step["outcome"]="push_failed"`, `report["steps"]["push"]`, `report["steps"]["local_dev_restore"] = _restore_local_dev_after_failed_push(...)`.
- `ruff check --select TRY004` reports **exactly one** finding repo-wide: `implement.py:13609`.
- Line drift: the chore title/description say 13270; the raise is now at 13609 (file grew since the chore was minted).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` push error handling (lines 13542–13640); a new module-level prelude helper beside `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push`.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — convergence + exhausted-infrastructure coverage (lines ~348–412).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — `connection_closed` + `"git push to dev transport lost"` message assertions (~lines 832–900).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_transport_keepalive.py` — "transport lost"/"not a test failure" message assertions (~lines 184–238).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py` — retry/evidence assertions (~lines 320–500).

## Related Work

- Parent audit finding: SA-0MW0V9PEP004EJYV (the audit run that produced this candidate).
- Duplicate closed: SA-0MWH1DCL60001JBL (raw lint chore for the same finding, stale line 13270) — closed as a duplicate of this item.
- Precedent: SA-0MWB1AYW0003DKQR (ruff ISC004 candidate accepted via waiver — the Option A route this item did **not** take).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk (behaviour drift):** the split must keep every observable unchanged. Mitigation: the existing tests already pin `outcome`, `reason`, both comment bodies and both message texts; extract the shared prelude into one helper so the split cannot diverge between clauses.
- **Risk (control flow):** the convergence branch currently `break`s out of an enclosing loop. A helper cannot `break`; it must return a sentinel (e.g. `True` = converged) and the caller `break`s. Verify the `break` target is preserved.
- **Risk (duplication):** a naive split duplicates ~40 lines. Mitigation: one prelude helper shared by both clauses (this is the planned shape, not two copies).
- **Assumption:** sibling relationship of the two exception classes (confirmed at 5012/5050) makes `except (A, B)` ≡ `except A:` + `except B:`; no catch-order hazard.
- **Assumption:** `ruff check --select TRY004` is the correct gate; the project runs no repo-wide ruff config today, so the AC asserts the explicit `--select`.

## Plan (Option B — refactor; test-first)

**Step 1 — test first (red).** Add a focused assertion that the file is TRY004-clean, e.g. in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py`: run `ruff check --select TRY004 --no-cache skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and assert exit 0 / no findings. It fails today (1 finding at 13609). Keep the existing regression tests untouched.

**Step 2 — extract the shared prelude.** Add a module-level helper next to `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push`, e.g.:

```python
def _finalise_failed_push(
    *, push_step, push_evidence, report, repo_root,
    commit_hash, parent_branch, local_dev_fast_forward,
) -> bool:
    """Record failure evidence and converge if the commit landed anyway.

    Returns True when the commit is verifiably on origin/dev (caller breaks
    out of the retry loop); False when the push genuinely failed.
    """
```
It performs: `push_step.update(_push_retry_trail_fields(push_evidence))`; `landed_now = _commit_is_on_origin_dev(...)`; on `landed_now["verified"]` set `success/outcome=already_pushed`, `report[...]`, `_set_finish_progress(...)` and return True; otherwise set `outcome="push_failed"`, `report["steps"]["push"]`, `report["steps"]["local_dev_restore"] = _restore_local_dev_after_failed_push(...)` and return False. Move the existing `LOG.warning` verbatim.

**Step 3 — split the handler.** Replace the single `except (PushTransportLostError, PushTransportExhaustedError) as exc:` with two sibling clauses, each building its own `push_step` dict (removing dispatch #1), calling `_finalise_failed_push(...)` and `break`ing when it returns True, then emitting its own comment + `raise RuntimeError(...) from exc` (messages copied verbatim; removing dispatch #2). Order the clauses `PushTransportLostError` first, then `PushTransportExhaustedError`.

**Step 4 — verify (green).** `ruff check --select TRY004 skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` → zero findings; the four push-transport test modules pass unchanged; then the full suite via `/skill:test` (never a bare pytest).

**Step 5 — close.** Record the commit hash in a comment, confirm `## Impact` is present, advance to `in_review`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (producer):** How should the TRY004 finding at `implement.py:13609` be resolved — Option A (audit waiver), Option B (refactor the `except`/dispatch), or Option C (`# noqa`)?
  - **A (producer, 2026-11-17): "1. B"** → **Option B — refactor** chosen. Final: Option B.
- **Q2 (secondary, Option A only):** line-scoped vs file-scoped waiver?
  - **Moot** — no waiver is recorded under Option B.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17 (`plan`, re-run — downtime dispatch): re-verified the plan against the current tree with no changes required. `ruff check --select TRY004 --no-cache skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` still reports **exactly one** finding at 13609 (single repo-wide finding; the raise is unchanged). Anchor lines are current: `except (PushTransportLostError, PushTransportExhaustedError)` at 13542, the two `isinstance(exc, PushTransportLostError)` dispatches at 13555/13602, `PushTransportLostError`/`PushTransportExhaustedError` as sibling `RuntimeError` subclasses at 5012/5050, `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push` at 8621 (helper placement anchor), and the `while True:` push-retry loop at ~13298 (the `break` target the sentinel must preserve). All five Key Files exist and `validate_key_files_format()` returns no errors; the four push-transport test modules pin `already_pushed`, `reason: connection_closed`, `outcome: push_failed` and the "git push to dev transport lost" message, so AC3 is verifiable unchanged. The AC coverage review proceeds (no children — single-step chore, correctly sized). Closed raw duplicate chore SA-0MWH1DCL60001JBL. Approval gate: not required (Small effort, Medium risk). The 2026-11-17 effort/risk estimate (`Small`/`Medium`, 3.67 h expected, 92% confidence) was produced against this same Option B plan and still stands unchanged. No children created — decomposition would be over-engineering.
- 2026-11-17 (`plan`): corrected the TRY004 rule description (was `error-messages-should-include-exception-class`; TRY004 is `type-check-without-type-error`); verified exactly one TRY004 finding repo-wide; recorded the producer's **Option B (refactor)** decision; rewrote AC1/AC2 from waiver-shape to refactor-shape; added the concrete test-first refactor plan (extract `_finalise_failed_push`, split the two sibling `except` clauses) and refactor-specific risks; identified the existing regression tests that pin behaviour. No children (single-step chore, correctly sized). Stage `plan_complete`; producer decision resolved.
- 2026-11-17 (`plan`, earlier): initial plan with Option A recommended; line reference 13270 → 13609.

## Goal

Define, before any implementation exists, the exact loader contract the
test-value aggregator must satisfy: how each upstream analyser's output is
read, normalised, and recorded as **present**, **absent** or **malformed**.

## Target outcome

A synthetic fixture set representing every upstream signal (plus its real
schema) and a failing-then-passing `test_loaders.py` that pins the contract.
This is the test-first half of the evidence-ingestion slice.

## Definition of done

- `skill/test-value/tests/fixtures/` holds minimal, hand-written JSON for:
  churn (`test_churn_data.json` shape: `metadata.analyser_version`,
  `file_stability.top_files[]` with `file`/`commits`/`total_additions`/
  `total_deletions`/`area`), mutation (`mutation_report.json` +
  `suite_source_map.json` planned shape), anti-pattern (per-file
  `{"file","verdict","reasons","summary"}` from
  `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py --json`), and optional
  runtime/flake data.
- Fixtures also cover the absent cases (file missing) and malformed cases
  (unknown schema version, non-JSON, missing required keys).
- `tests/test_loaders.py` fails (ImportError) until the loaders land, then
  passes. It asserts the three-way signal status, not "silently empty".
- No fixture embeds real repository paths; all are relative and portable.

## Constraints

- Read-only against any analysed project; fixtures must not shell out.
- Fixture schemas mirror the current upstream output exactly; a schema change
  upstream must show up as a deliberate fixture edit, not silent inference.
- Do not import the upstream analysers to *generate* fixtures — hand-written
  fixtures keep the aggregator's contract decoupled from upstream internals.

## Risky assumptions

- The mutation schema (`mutation_report.json`, `suite_source_map.json`) is
  planned by `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` and not yet landed, so the fixture encodes
  *the documented plan*, not observed output. If the landed schema differs the
  fixture is updated as a deliberate change (documented in the item).
- The churn per-file signal only covers `file_stability.top_files` (top 20
  feature-commit-churned files), so "absent" is the common case for most test
  files — the contract must model that explicitly rather than infer churn 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fixtures exist for churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime signals, plus absent and malformed variants of each.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts present/absent/malformed status for every signal type.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts malformed input surfaces an explicit loader error naming the signal and reason — never a silent empty result.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts relative-path normalisation and deterministic ordering of loaded per-file records.
- `test_loaders.py` asserts loading does not recompute any churn, mutation or anti-pattern metric (values flow through unchanged).

## Key Files

- `skill/test-value/tests/conftest.py` — Loads the aggregator modules by path and exposes fixture paths.
- `skill/test-value/tests/fixtures/churn_data.json` — Synthetic churn analyser output.

None — this is the first test-first item. Blocks the loader implementation.

# Add classification tests: JSON-emitting fake runner

## Problem
The existing gate tests (`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) use a fake runner that only records invocations and returns an exit code. They cannot exercise the JSON classification path, so nothing pins the new `gate_reason` behaviour.

## Solution
Extend the test fixture in `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` with a JSON-emitting fake runner that produces structured results matching `run_tests.py`'s `--json` output shape, and assert that `merge-dev-to-main.sh` classifies each correctly.

### Test cases
- **Green suite**: runner emits `{"failures": [], "exit_code": 0}` → gate prints "full suite green" and exits 0.
- **Test failure**: runner emits `{"failures": [{"name": "test_foo"}], "exit_code": 1}` → gate prints `gate_reason=test_failure`, exits non-zero.
- **Slot contention**: runner emits `{"notice_codes": ["slot_busy"], "failures": [], "exit_code": 1}` → gate prints `gate_reason=slot_contention` with the wait-then-retry / raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` hint, exits non-zero.
- **Killed run**: runner emits `{"notice_codes": ["killed"], "failures": [], "exit_code": 1}` → gate prints `gate_reason=killed`, exits non-zero.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1 — Hermetic test pins the classification: a test in `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (or a new test file) exercises the classifier against a fake runner that produces JSON results for slot contention, killed, and red-suite cases, asserting the correct `gate_reason` and diagnostic output.
- AC2 — Green-suite case: runner emits success JSON → the gate prints "Release gate: full suite green" and exits 0.
- AC3 — Test-failure case: runner emits structured failures → the gate prints `gate_reason=test_failure` and the red-suite remediation, exits non-zero, creates no PR.
- AC4 — Slot-contention case: runner emits a `slot_busy` notice → the gate prints `gate_reason=slot_contention` with the wait-then-retry / raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` hint, exits non-zero.
- AC5 — Killed-run case: runner emits a `killed` notice → the gate prints `gate_reason=killed` with the killed remediation, exits non-zero.

## Constraints
- UK English.
- Reuse the existing test fixture pattern (`_build_release_fixture`, `_run_release`) — isolated `HOME`, fake runner, fake `gh`.
- No ad-hoc suite invocations; the tests are hermetic and run through the test skill.
- Written first (expected red) against the modified `merge-dev-to-main.sh`.

## Key Files
- `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` — new classification test cases go here.
- `skill/test/scripts/gate_reason.py` — the classifier under test.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — the modified script under test.

## Dependencies
- None. Blocks the implementation slice (`SA-0MWIT20V9004VBR6`): the tests are written first (red) and the implementation makes them green.

# End-to-end Python detection pipeline

Deliver a working, runnable near-duplicate detector for Python test files: AST extraction, normalisation, shingle/Jaccard similarity, inverted index, basic clustering, CLI, and JSON + Markdown output. This is the tracer-bullet slice — it goes from test-file collection through to written reports in one deliverable.

## Parent AC coverage

This task covers **AC1 (structural detection)** — Python test blocks detected via ast with docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches; never raw text equality. Also covers **AC2 (clusters reported with location and score)** for the Python path — each cluster lists member file paths, start-end line ranges, block sizes, similarity scores and redundancy measure; JSON + Markdown written to --output-dir. Also covers **AC4 (performance bounds)** — inverted shingle index used instead of all-pairs; --min-lines, --threshold defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 - Detection is structural, not textual. Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via ast (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure. (This slice delivers the Python part; JS/TS follows in the next slice.)
- AC2 - Clusters are reported with location and score. Each cluster lists every member's file path, start-end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both test_duplicates.json (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and test_duplicate_report.md (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to --output-dir. (This slice delivers the Python path end-to-end.)
- AC3 - Python block extraction: top-level functions, classes, methods, and with-wrapped test bodies are extracted with file path and start-end line range.
- AC4 - Python normalisation: docstrings removed, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders per lexical scope, literals canonicalised to type placeholders (string to {str}, int to {int}, etc.), whitespace collapsed.
- AC5 - Token k-gram shingle generation (k default 5), Jaccard similarity, and inverted shingle index producing candidate pairs without all-pairs O(n^2) comparison.
- AC6 - Basic transitive clustering of blocks above threshold, redundancy measure (member lines minus largest member lines), clusters ordered by total redundant lines descending.
- AC7 - CLI accepts: --project-root, --output-dir, --min-lines N, --threshold, and --quiet. Shaped like the churn analyser CLI.
- AC8 - test_duplicate_report.md and test_duplicates.json written with method, thresholds, limitations and cluster data; one-line summary printed to stderr.
- AC9 - Output is deterministic: same tree and flags produce byte-identical JSON; non-deterministic sources (file system order) are sorted.
- AC10 - Unit tests cover: Python AST extraction of async tests, parametrised tests and nested classes; normalisation invariance (renamed copy scores >= threshold); distinct behaviour below band; shingle and Jaccard behaviour; inverted index correctness; basic clustering and redundant-line arithmetic; JSON and Markdown schema/content; deterministic output; empty/single-block suite.
- AC11 - skill/test-churn/SKILL.md gains a Near-duplicate detection section and docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md gains a skeleton recording the method and thresholds; both updated in this slice, not deferred.

## Deliverables

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - Python extraction, normalisation, shingling, Jaccard, inverted index, basic clustering, CLI, JSON/MD writers
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - unit + e2e tests for the Python pipeline
- skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py - path-loaded fixture for test_duplicate_detection
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md - Near-duplicate detection section
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md - method and thresholds skeleton

## Key Files

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - extract_blocks_python(), normalise_python_ast(), generate_shingles(), jaccard_similarity(), build_inverted_index(), cluster_blocks(), write_json_report(), write_md_report(), main()
- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py - reuse is_test_file() and ChurnConfig
- skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py - fixture loader
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - Python pipeline tests
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md - new section
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md - method skeleton

## Dependencies

None - this is the first vertical slice.

## Problem statement

AUDIT-FP-WAIVER markers recorded via `audit_waiver.py add` are compared to ruff findings by exact string match on the file path (`_matching_waiver` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`). Ruff's JSON output carries absolute filenames (e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/report/tests/test_check_producer_actions.py`), but waivers are commonly recorded with repo-relative paths (e.g. `skill/report/tests/test_check_producer_actions.py`). Result: the waiver never matches the finding, so the audit keeps minting fresh CFP chores every run. Verified: for the ISC004 waivers on parent SA-0MVYEZ3V3004AQXN (lines 152/155/160), `_matching_waiver` returned no match for any of the three lines despite the waivers existing.

Discovered from: SA-0MWB8VYAP008H6VX (producer decision Q2 → Option B, comment SA-C0MWJ67LYG006S369).

## Users

- Producers accepting false positives via `audit_waiver.py add`.
- The audit system: accepted findings must stop generating CFP chores and stop entering the producer-review queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_matching_waiver` treats repo-relative and machine-absolute forms of the same file as equivalent (normalises both sides before comparison; e.g. via the existing `_repo_relative_path` helper or a shared normaliser).
2. A waiver recorded with a repo-relative path suppresses a finding carrying the absolute path, and vice versa (round-trip normalisation).
3. Line-matched waivers still match the same line only; rule/linter matching semantics unchanged; a whole-file waiver (no line) still matches any line.
4. Unit tests cover: relative-vs-absolute match, absolute-vs-relative match, mismatched rule still not waived, and no regression on `test_audit_runner_cfp_dedup_waiver.py`.
5. `ruff` and the audit unit tests pass; no behaviour change for findings already matched by exact paths.

## Impact

Producers can record waivers with whichever path form they have to hand and the audit will actually honour them — no more phantom CFP chores for already-accepted false positives.

## Constraints

- Fix in the audit runner's matching layer (`_matching_waiver` and/or a shared path normaliser); do not change ruff's emission.
- Do not alter the existing `AUDIT-FP-WAIVER` comment marker format or the `audit_waiver.py` CLI contract.
